## Problem

When a new project is created (or an existing one initialized) with an AGENTS.md, the current installer/template behavior emits the full duplicated instruction set as a local file. This is how the four sibling projects ended up with large local AGENTS.md files that duplicate the global one (see SA-0MSITKHPW002XG4G, SA-0MSITKOXI007XD4N).

## User story

As a developer creating a new project, I want the AGENTS.md installer to emit only the canonical global-reference structure so new projects never start by duplicating the global rules.

## Desired change

Improve the tooling/template that creates AGENTS.md for a project so the generated local file contains only the canonical structure (as adopted by SorraAgents itself in SA-0MSIUUYRD002GC8W):

    ## Global agent guidance

    Read the global agent instructions at ~/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md — they define the core principles, the Worklog (wl) work-item workflow, and the coding disciplines that apply to every project.

    ## Project-specific guidance

    (project-specific rules are added by the project owner here, never by copying the global file)

- Locate the installer/template mechanism (search scripts, wl/pi project init, templates dir, .pi scaffolding) and change the emitted template.
- The canonical structure is emitted by default; project-specific rules are added by the project owner on top, never by copying the global file.
- If the installer supports an option to copy the global file (e.g. for offline/standalone use), keep it as an explicit opt-in.
- Coordinate with the Worklog side: ContextHub wl init should delegate agent-guidance/workflow setup to the SorraAgents install rather than duplicating it (tracked in ContextHub work item WL-0MSIXMKOX0052514).

## Acceptance criteria

1. The installer/template that creates AGENTS.md now emits exactly the canonical structure above (## Global agent guidance reference + ## Project-specific guidance placeholder).
2. Creating a fresh project (or re-running init) produces an AGENTS.md whose content is the canonical structure, not a copy of the global file.
3. Existing behavior for projects with custom local rules is unaffected (they keep their local rules below the reference line).
4. Any docs describing the installer and the global-vs-project AGENTS.md split are updated.
5. Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Key Files

- TBD at plan time: search for AGENTS.md templates/installers (e.g. ~/.pi/agent/ scaffolding, pi init, project setup scripts). Candidate locations: ~/.pi/agent/settings.json, /usr/local/lib/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/ (pi's own project init), any templates/ dirs in ~/.pi/agent/.

- related-to:SA-0MSITKOXI007XD4N (sibling projects AGENTS.md dedup)

# 24h experiment: AGENTS.md STE100 instruction — session length & token use vs previous period

## Problem statement

We want empirical evidence on whether instructing agents to "Always use ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English" changes agent efficiency. Currently unmeasured. This work item runs a controlled 24-hour experiment: add the instruction to the global AGENTS.md, measure session length and token usage per session over the 24h window, compare against the previous 24h window, then revert.

## Users

- **Operator (Ralph)** — wants to know whether an STE-style output constraint affects session duration and token consumption (cost proxy) before deciding whether to adopt it permanently.

User story:
- As an operator, I want a before/after comparison of session length and token use so that I can decide whether "Always use ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English." in AGENTS.md is worth keeping.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Treatment applied and verified:** `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` (symlinked to `~/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md`) contains exactly the sentence "Always use ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English." during the experiment window, and is reverted after the window. Both states verified via `grep` (before, during, after).
2. **Baseline metrics computed:** for the 24h period immediately preceding the experiment start (T0), computed from session logs for **all projects**: session count, mean/median session length (minutes), mean/median total tokens per session, input/output/cache breakdown, total tokens, and total cost where recorded.
3. **Experiment metrics computed:** same metrics for the window [T0, T0+24h), sessions attributed to the window by session start timestamp.
4. **Comparison report produced and committed:** delta % and direction for each metric (duration, total tokens, input tokens, output tokens), notable outliers (e.g. sessions with output-token-limit errors), project and model breakdown, and a one-line interpretation per metric. Report lives in the repo (e.g. `docs/experiments/ste100-24h/report.md`).
5. **Reproducible measurement:** a single command re-runs the full analysis over the session-log directory and produces identical results (deterministic). If the measurement is delegated to the proxy's usage tooling, verify that tooling actually exists and runs; otherwise the analysis script in this repo is the source of truth (validated during intake: session logs contain per-message `usage` with input/output/cacheRead/cacheWrite/totalTokens/cost).
6. **All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes (README/wiki entries, code comments in the analysis script).
7. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes** (including any tests added for the analysis script).

## Constraints

- **Bare sentence only** — the literal instruction "Always use ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English." No rule expansion, no dictionary, no enforcement tooling.
- **Global scope** — the change lands in `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` (affects every project). This is intended; the change MUST be reverted after the window.
- **Do not modify** session logs, proxy configuration, or any other project's files.
- **Measurement scope:** all sessions across all projects (per operator decision).
- STE *compliance* measurement (whether outputs actually follow STE) is **out of scope** — this experiment measures only session length and token use. Any compliance sampling should be a separate work item (scope-creep guard).
- Changes to `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` follow the repo's normal workflow: implemented in a worktree, committed to `dev` (never `main`), even though this is a temporary experiment. The symlink `~/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md → AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` means no install step is needed; the instruction takes effect for sessions *started after* the change lands.

## Existing state

- `~/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md` is a symlink to `/home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents/AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` (verified).
- Session logs at `~/.pi/agent/sessions/<project-slug>/*.jsonl` contain: a `session` header event (start timestamp, cwd, id) and per-message assistant events with a `usage` object (`input`, `output`, `cacheRead`, `cacheWrite`, `totalTokens`, `cost`). Last event timestamp ≈ session end. Verified during intake.
- Baseline sample (SorraAgents sessions only, 2026-08-09): 69 sessions, ~30.5h total, avg 26.6 min/session, avg 3.8M total tokens/session (dominated by cache reads; total-token values include cache). One extreme outlier session (153 min, 146.9M total tokens) associated with repeated output-token-limit errors — the report must handle such outliers (report both mean and median).
- `skill/proxy-usage-analysis/` exists but currently contains **no source files** (only `__pycache__`). If this is the "existing usage skill in the proxy" intended for measurement, it must be verified to actually run; otherwise the analysis script in this work item is authoritative.
- `skill/context-audit/scripts/measure_context.py` measures startup-context bytes — related (our change grows startup context by ~50 bytes) but does not measure session token usage. Run before/after to confirm the addition stays within `docs/dev/context-budget.thresholds.json` if that gate is enforced.

## Desired change

1. Add the sentence to `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` in the worktree; commit to `dev`; record exact commit hash and wall-clock T0.
2. Let the experiment run 24h (T0 → T0+24h). No special agent behavior needed during the window beyond normal work.
3. At T0+24h: collect metrics for [T0−24h, T0) and [T0, T0+24h) across all projects; produce the comparison report; revert the AGENTS_GLOBAL.md change (new commit to `dev`); record revert hash.
4. Deliver: report (metrics table, deltas, outliers, interpretation), AC verification, session-log of the experiment itself.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` — add then revert the STE sentence (the treatment).
- `docs/experiments/ste100-24h/report.md` — comparison report (new).
- `skill/ste100-experiment/scripts/analyze_sessions.py` (new, or revived `skill/proxy-usage-analysis/`) — deterministic analysis over `~/.pi/agent/sessions/**/*.jsonl`; produces per-session duration/tokens and window aggregates + tests.
- `skill/proxy-usage-analysis/` — verify/revive if the proxy-side usage skill is to be used for measurement.

## Related work

- `SA-0MSJI53RX006E2PS` / `SA-0MSJI50Y9005VECR` — "Reduce initial LLM context…" (completed + in-progress): same file (`AGENTS_GLOBAL.md`), context-budget angle. Our +1 sentence slightly increases startup context; keep within budget.
- `SA-0MSLK72KI006N9KP` (F1) — "Startup-context measurement tooling": produced `skill/context-audit/scripts/measure_context.py`; related measurement tooling, different axis.
- `SA-0MSISKM8F004NW1U` — "Reduce audit skill initial session context size": also touches startup-context surface.
- `skill/proxy-usage-analysis/` — intended measurement tool per operator; source currently missing, verify.
- `SA-0MSI51QTA009WDFO` — "Add session logging instruction to AGENTS.md" (in-progress): same file (`AGENTS_GLOBAL.md`); session-traceability comments are how experiment sessions get identified/attributed.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Null result risk:** a bare STE100 sentence may not change model output measurably (no vocabulary enforcement; model may not deeply know STE rules). A null result is a valid outcome — report it as such rather than extending the experiment.
- **Confounds:** session mix (project, work type, human vs automated, model, token-limit error loops) differs between windows; day-of-week/time-of-day effects. Mitigations: report medians alongside means, break down by project/model, describe composition, keep interpretation descriptive (correlation, not causation).
- **Boundary sessions:** sessions spanning T0 or T0+24h attributed by *start timestamp* (documented rule).
- **Measurement tooling uncertainty:** if the proxy usage skill is non-functional, the repo analysis script (AC 5) is authoritative — do not block on proxy tooling.
- **Left-over instruction:** the sentence must be reverted; AC 1 greps verify both states. Add a calendar/reminder if available to avoid the window overrunning.
- **Scope creep:** STE compliance scoring, dictionary enforcement, or policy changes are separate work items (`discovered-from:SA-0MSMC8KRS00164VD` if created).

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MLGALPU80E5HBIJ** – Persist pending prompts to tool-output (completed)
- **SA-0MSI51QTA009WDFO** – Add session logging instruction to AGENTS.md (in-progress)
- **SA-0MM03YIY609CP27Y** – Scheduler Test Button Command (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `.worklog/tmp/intake-draft-ste100-experiment-SA-0MSMC8KRS00164VD.md` — matched: 24h, agent, agents, always, asd (+21 more)
- `.worklog/worktrees/wl-SA-0MSLK7LGA003J0KP-compact-agents-global-md-to-8-kb-f4/skill/audit/SKILL.md` — matched: agent, agents, always, bare, decisions (+13 more)
- `.worklog/worktrees/wl-SA-0MSLK7LGA003J0KP-compact-agents-global-md-to-8-kb-f4/skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: agent, agents, always, bare, decisions (+13 more)

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Which AGENTS.md gets the instruction? (a) Global AGENTS_GLOBAL.md — affects every session in every project, most representative; (b) SorraAgents project AGENTS.md only — contained blast radius." — Answer (user): "1. Global". Source: interactive reply 2026-08-09.
- Q2: "Measurement scope: (a) All sessions across all projects, or (b) only sessions in the project(s) whose AGENTS.md carries the instruction?" — Answer (user): "2. All (existing usage skill in the proxy will measure this)". Source: interactive reply 2026-08-09. Note: intake could not locate a functional proxy usage skill — only `skill/proxy-usage-analysis/` with no source files; AC 5 requires verifying that path or falling back to the repo analysis script.
- Q3: "Instruction fidelity: keep the literal sentence only, or append a short key-rule expansion?" — Answer (user): "3. Bare sentence". Source: interactive reply 2026-08-09.

## Assumptions recorded

- T0 = wall-clock time the AGENTS_GLOBAL.md change lands on `dev` (commit time). Baseline = [T0−24h, T0). Experiment = [T0, T0+24h).
- "Previous period" = the immediately preceding 24h window (not same-weekday-matched). Day-of-week parity noted as a reporting nicety, not a requirement.
- Cost metrics used only where the log records `cost`; primary metric is `totalTokens` with input/output/cache breakdown as secondary.

Roll out the F6 context-budget regression gate (SA-0MSLK7XNZ00366YY) to every project using the installed pi framework. Today only SorraAgents has the v2 pre-push hook with the gate; the other 6 framework projects (ampa, ContextHub, dev-scripts, llm-manager, open_source_llm, Tableau-Card-Engine) carry v1 hooks (worklog sync only) and none except Tableau-Card-Engine sets `core.hooksPath`.

Current state (verified 2026-08-10):

| Project | .githooks/pre-push | core.hooksPath |
|---|---|---|
| SorraAgents | v2 (gate + sync) | unset |
| ampa | v1 | unset |
| ContextHub | v1 | unset |
| dev-scripts | v1 | unset |
| llm-manager | v1 | unset |
| open_source_llm | v1 | unset |
| Tableau-Card-Engine | v1 | .githooks |

Two structural gaps beyond simple hook rollout:

1. **Tooling resolution:** the v2 hook resolves `measure_context.py` from `$repo_root/skill/context-audit/...` — a path that exists ONLY in SorraAgents. The installed framework symlinks the skill into `~/.pi/agent/skills/context-audit/scripts/measure_context.py` (via `scripts/install_pi.sh`), so other projects would silently fail-open unless the hook falls back to the global path.
2. **Per-project thresholds:** `docs/dev/context-budget.thresholds.json` is SorraAgents-specific (global_agents=8192, project_agents=1334, skills_prose=3523, total=13049). Each project has different AGENTS.md / skills sizes and needs its own measured baseline + committed thresholds, or the gate is meaningless.

The global AGENTS_GLOBAL.md is symlinked to all projects, so the ~54% compaction benefit propagates — the gate protects that investment repo-wide.

## Target outcome

Every framework project's push to `dev` runs the context-budget gate with project-appropriate thresholds; a change that regresses startup context beyond budget is blocked locally before reaching `dev`, everywhere.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: v2 pre-push hook resolves `measure_context.py` via the installed global symlink (`~/.pi/agent/skills/context-audit/scripts/measure_context.py`) when no local `skill/context-audit/` exists, still fail-open only when the framework is absent entirely.
- AC2: A repeatable per-project baseline flow (script or documented commands) measures each project's startup context and emits a project thresholds file (e.g. `docs/dev/context-budget.thresholds.json` or `.pi-config/`), committed to that project.
- AC3: The v2 hook + gate is installed/wired in all 6 non-SorraAgents framework projects (via `core.hooksPath .githooks` or hook install), verified end-to-end with a simulated push in at least one non-SorraAgents project.
- AC4: Worklog sync behavior is preserved in every project (no regression from v1→v2 switch).
- AC5: `scripts/install_pi.sh` (or a sibling helper) propagates the hook/global tooling so future projects get the gate automatically; docs updated (e.g. `docs/dev/context-budget.md` or a new docs page).
- AC6: Full test suite in SorraAgents remains green (pytest + Node), including `tests/test_context_budget_gate.py` and pre-push hook tests.

## Minimal implementation

- Update `.githooks/pre-push` v2 to fall back to the global symlink path for the measure script.
- Add a baseline/generate-thresholds helper (extend `measure_context.py` or a small script) that snapshots per-project components into a thresholds JSON.
- Install v2 hook + `core.hooksPath` in the 6 other projects; generate + commit per-project thresholds.
- Extend `scripts/install_pi.sh` to also link/wire hooks (or document the one-time per-project setup).
- Update docs.

## Dependencies

- F6 (SA-0MSLK7XNZ00366YY) — gate tooling + SorraAgents thresholds committed.
- SA-0MSN2LIOQ004TON1 — activates the gate in SorraAgents first (this item generalizes the same mechanism).

## Deliverables

- Global-resolution v2 hook (works in any framework project)
- Per-project thresholds for all 6 projects
- Gate wired + verified in all framework projects
- Installer/docs updates

## Notes

- Discovered while following up on F6 audit variance (AC3).
- Not blocking: gate already enforced in SorraAgents via the pytest suite; this extends protection repo-wide.

## Summary
run_tests.py (skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py) resolves its target repo from its OWN install location (REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3] = the SorraAgents framework repo), not from the invoking project. The CLI (main -> run_all without cwd -> cwd = cwd or REPO_ROOT) therefore runs/caches the FRAMEWORK repo's suite when invoked from any other project.

## Evidence (from llm repo, cwd=/home/rgardler/projects/llm)
- 'python3 /home/rgardler/.pi/agent/skills/test/scripts/run_tests.py --summary --suite pytest' printed '8 failed, 1814 passed' — that is the SORRAAGENTS suite (llm's suite is 2130 passed, exit 0).
- '--json --suite pytest' returned cached=True returncode=1 — reading the SorraAgents cache, not the llm cache.
- The audit skill compensates correctly: TARGET_PROJECT_ROOT = git rev-parse --show-toplevel at import; passes cwd=str(project_root) to query_cached/run_cached, so the llm cache entries are written/read via the audit path only.

## Impact
An agent or operator following the test skill's documented invocation (python3 ./scripts/run_tests.py --json) from a non-framework project tests and caches the WRONG repo's suite. Cross-project consumers must remember to pass cwd explicitly (audit does; ship/implement pass cwd where relevant).

## Proposed fix (minimal)
Detect the invoking project root from cwd at CLI time — e.g. 'git rev-parse --show-toplevel' from os.getcwd() when --cwd is not passed (mirroring audit_runner.TARGET_PROJECT_ROOT), falling back to REPO_ROOT. Preserve existing behavior when invoked from the framework repo itself. Alternatively add a --project-root flag and document it in the test skill SKILL.md.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] run_tests.py CLI run from a non-framework project (e.g. llm) targets that project's repo + cache (git-state fingerprint at that project's HEAD), not SorraAgents.
- [ ] Invoked from the framework repo itself, behavior is unchanged.
- [ ] Audit skill read-only auto-verification (query_cached at TARGET_PROJECT_ROOT) still hits the same cache entries.
- [ ] Test skill SKILL.md documents the project-root resolution (and any --project-root flag).

# Audit Skill: Add Descriptive `--session-id` to Pi Subprocess Invocations

## Problem statement

The audit skill spawns `pi` subprocesses via two code paths (`audit_runner.py` and `audit_pr.py`) but does not pass `--session-id`. This means audit sessions are auto-generated UUIDs that cannot be traced back to the work item being audited, making debugging, session review, and audit traceability difficult.

## Users

- **Auditors/reviewers** — can locate the exact pi session for a given audit by WL ID
- **Operators debugging audit failures** — can inspect `PI_SESSION_ID` and find the session file
- **Maintainers of the audit skill** — can distinguish between concurrent audit runs

**Example user stories:**

- As an operator, I want the pi session created by `audit_runner.py` to carry `--session-id audit-SA-0MSABC123_phase2-abc12345` so I can find it in `~/.pi/agent/sessions/` for debugging.
- As a reviewer, I want audit sessions to be uniquely named per invocation (not per WL item) so I can see all retries and retry-specific context in their own sessions.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `audit_runner.py` — `_call_pi()` adds `--session-id audit-{issue_id}-{context}-{uuid}` to the pi command. The `context` parameter (e.g., `phase2_deep`, `parent`, `child:SA-XXX`, `verdict_reask`, `project`) is forwarded as the phase segment. The UUID is 8 hex chars (`uuid4().hex[:8]`), fresh per invocation.

2. `audit_pr.py` — `run_audit_in_worktree()` adds `--session-id audit-{wl_id}-entrypoint-{uuid}` (8 hex chars UUID, fresh per invocation). Only applied when not in `dry_run` mode.

3. The session-id format adheres to `--session-id` constraints: starts/ends with alphanumeric, contains only alphanumeric, `-`, `_`, `.` (verified by `assertValidSessionId`). Colons in context values (e.g., `child:SA-XXX`) are replaced with underscores.

4. The existing `--no-context-files --no-skills` context-reduction flags are preserved unchanged.

5. All existing tests pass, including updated mocks that verify `--session-id` is present in the command args and contains the correct WL ID.

## Constraints

- Audit skill only — no other skills spawn `pi` subprocesses.
- The session-id must not interfere with `--no-session` (if used anywhere).
- UUID must be generated at call time (per-invocation uniqueness for retry visibility).
- Must not change the command semantics — only add an additional flag.
- `audit_pr.py`: `--session-id` is only added when `dry_run=False`.

## Existing state

Two `pi` invocation sites in the audit skill:

| File | Line | Function | Phase context |
|------|------|----------|---------------|

# Skills: tag pi sessions spawned from skills with --session-id

## Problem statement

Every pi session spawned from within a skill — the audit skill's `_call_pi()` in `audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` and `run_audit_in_worktree()` in `audit/audit_pr.py` — is saved under pi's default random session ID, so when debugging an audit run it is impossible to tell which session belongs to which work item or which phase produced it. Skills should pass `--session-id` so every spawned pi session clearly identifies the work item it is for and the action being taken (e.g. `audit-{id}-{phase}-{uuid}`).

## Users

- **Producers/operators** debugging audit runs: want to identify, resume, and inspect the exact pi session for a given work item and phase (`pi --session <id>` / `/resume`).
- **Audit skill maintainers**: want session-per-call isolation (unique ID per call) so parallel/fan-out pi calls never share a session file and never re-trigger the "Cannot continue from message role: assistant" failure mode.
- **Operators of long-running systems**: want stale skill-spawned sessions pruned automatically so `~/.pi/agent/sessions/` does not grow unboundedly.

### Example user stories

- As a producer, I want each pi session spawned during an audit to carry `--session-id audit-{work_item_id}-{phase}-{short_uuid}`, so I can resume the exact session that produced a failed verdict.
- As a maintainer, I want each call to get a unique session (not a shared one), so repeated calls never append into the same session file and never hit the assistant-role continuation error that Ralph's original `--no-session` fix addressed.
- As an operator, I want `audit-*` sessions older than a retention period automatically pruned after each audit run, so the session store stays bounded.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Every pi subprocess spawned by the audit skill passes `--session-id` with a unique per-call value. `_call_pi()` in `audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` appends `--session-id <id>` to the constructed command; the value is generated in `_call_pi_and_maybe_log()` as `audit-{work_item_id}-{context}-{short_uuid}` (short uuid = `uuid4().hex[:8]`).
- [ ] `audit/audit_pr.py` `run_audit_in_worktree()` passes `--session-id audit-pr-{wl_id}-{short_uuid}` for each spawned pi call.
- [ ] Session IDs are unique per call — no two calls share a session file; session-per-call isolation means no "Cannot continue from message role: assistant" errors are introduced.
- [ ] Project-level audits (no work-item id) use a stable placeholder in the id (`audit-project-{short_uuid}` — dedupe the repeated `project` context so the id reads cleanly).
- [ ] Automatic cleanup runs at the end of an audit run (`issue` and `project` commands): session files whose names match the `audit-` prefix and whose mtime is older than the retention period (default 112 days) are pruned from the pi session directory.
- [ ] Retention is configurable via a `--session-retention-days` CLI flag on both subcommands and/or an `AUDIT_SESSION_RETENTION_DAYS` env var (flag wins).
- [ ] Cleanup is conservative: it only removes `audit-`-prefixed sessions — never other pi sessions.
- [ ] Tests verify: (a) `--session-id` appears in every constructed pi command with the expected format, (b) session ids are unique across calls, (c) cleanup prunes only stale `audit-*` files and honors the retention setting, (d) existing cmd-construction tests (e.g. `TestCallPiEnableTools`) are updated and still pass.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md`, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Follow the established Ralph session-per-call precedent (SA-0MQ6E8NCG003STJB): unique `--session-id` per call, dash-separated `{skill}-{work_item_id}-{phase}-{short_uuid}` format, conservative prefix-scoped cleanup, default retention 112 days.
- Backward compatible: `_call_pi()` gains an optional `session_id: str | None = None` parameter; when unset the command is byte-identical to today (existing direct callers/tests unaffected).
- Cleanup must never touch sessions that do not start with the `audit-` prefix.
- The audit skill's context-reduction invariants (`--no-context-files --no-skills`, self-contained prompts) are untouched.
- `CHANGELOG.md` is excluded (managed by the ship skill release pipeline).

## Existing state

- `audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` `_call_pi()` (line ~1492): `cmd = [pi_bin, "-p", "--mode", "json", "--model", model, prompt]` (+ optional `--tools`, always `--no-context-files --no-skills`). Sessions are saved under pi's default random IDs.
- `_call_pi_and_maybe_log(issue_id, context, prompt, ...)` (line ~2816) already threads `issue_id` (a work-item id, a child id, or `"project"`) and `context` (e.g. `parent`, `phase2_deep`, `child_ac_fallback`) for debug-log naming, but does not forward them to `_call_pi()`.
- `audit/audit_pr.py` `run_audit_in_worktree()` (line ~192): `cmd = ['pi', '-p', '--mode', 'json', f"/audit {wl_id}"]` — `wl_id` is in scope.
- No `--session-id` usage exists anywhere in the skill tree today.
- Session storage: pi saves to `~/.pi/agent/sessions/--<path-slug>--/` (overridable via `PI_CODING_AGENT_SESSION_DIR` / `--session-dir`); cleanup should honor the env/flag override when present.
- Existing cmd-construction tests in `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner.py` (e.g. `TestCallPiEnableTools`, ~lines 290–400) assert exact arg lists (`assert args == ["pi", "-p", ...]`) and must be updated.
- No dedicated `audit_pr.py` test file exists; add session-id coverage there or in the audit runner tests.

## Desired change

1. **`_call_pi()`**: add optional `session_id: str | None = None`; when set, append `--session-id <session_id>` to the command (before/with the context-reduction flags).
2. **`_call_pi_and_maybe_log()`**: build `session_id = f"audit-{issue_id}-{context}-{uuid4().hex[:8]}"` and forward to `_call_pi()`.
3. **`audit_pr.py`**: build `f"audit-pr-{wl_id}-{uuid4().hex[:8]}"` and append `--session-id`.
4. **Cleanup**: add a helper that scans the pi session directory (honoring `PI_CODING_AGENT_SESSION_DIR`/`--session-dir`) for files whose name starts with `audit-`, prunes those older than the retention period (default 112 days; `--session-retention-days` flag + `AUDIT_SESSION_RETENTION_DAYS` env), and logs pruned count/space. Invoke after `issue` and `project` audit commands complete.
5. **Tests**: update cmd-construction tests; add format/uniqueness assertions and cleanup tests (stale pruning, prefix scoping, retention config precedence).
6. **Docs**: update `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` and code comments documenting the session-id convention and retention.

## Key Files:

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `_call_pi()` (~line 1492) add `--session-id` support; `_call_pi_and_maybe_log()` (~line 2816) generate `audit-{id}-{context}-{short_uuid}`; `main()`/`cmd_issue`/`cmd_project` add `--session-retention-days` + cleanup hook
- `skill/audit/audit_pr.py` — `run_audit_in_worktree()` (~line 192) add `--session-id audit-pr-{wl_id}-{short_uuid}`
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner.py` — update `TestCallPiEnableTools` cmd assertions; add session-id format/uniqueness + cleanup tests
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — document session-id convention + retention config

## Related work

- **SA-0MQ6E8NCG003STJB** — "Ralph: Use session-per-call with unique IDs instead of --no-session" (completed): direct precedent — `--session-id` per call, `{skill}-{id}-{phase}-{short_uuid}` format, 112-day retention cleanup, prefix-scoped pruning.
- **SA-0MQ533A3M003N3ER** — "Document how to execute skills via CLI" (completed): documents the session-per-call pattern for pi subprocess invocations.
- **SA-0MPFD4RWQ009AXJR** — Ralph "Cannot continue from message role: assistant" (completed): the original shared-session failure this design avoids by using unique IDs per call.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope creep**: session tagging could expand to every conceivable pi invocation or to a shared `pi_utils` helper refactor. Mitigation: scope is limited to the two existing spawn points; extra ideas are recorded as follow-up work items, not scope.
- **Session accumulation**: unique-per-call sessions accumulate faster than shared ones. Mitigation: retention cleanup is included in this item (default 112 days, `audit-` prefix only).
- **Filename/ID character safety**: work-item ids and context strings are filename-safe alphanumerics/dashes; no sanitization needed beyond the prefix convention.
- **Behavioral change risk**: adding a flag to every spawned command could interact with `--mode json` streaming. Mitigation: identical invocation to Ralph's proven pattern; tests assert command structure; backward-compatible default (`None`).
- **Assumption**: retention default of 112 days and the `--session-retention-days` flag naming follow the Ralph precedent; configurable via env var `AUDIT_SESSION_RETENTION_DAYS` (no config-file migration needed since the audit skill has no `.ralph.json`-style config).

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Session ID uniqueness — shared `audit_<id>` per work item (matches your `intake_<id>` example) vs Ralph-style unique per call (`audit-{id}-{phase}-{short_uuid}`)?" — Answer (user): **1b — Ralph-style unique per call** (`audit-{work_item_id}-{context}-{short_uuid}`), dash-separated. Source: interactive reply.
- Q2: "Scope — audit skill only, all current skill pi-spawn points, or audit + documented convention?" — Answer (user): **2b — all current skill pi-spawn points**. Research: a full-tree scan found exactly two spawn points, both in the audit skill: `audit_runner.py::_call_pi` and `audit_pr.py::run_audit_in_worktree`. Source: interactive reply + repo grep.
- Q3: "Cleanup — include session retention pruning in this item or keep out of scope?" — Answer (user): **include in this item**. Source: interactive reply.

# Pane title status indicator on skill completion

## Problem statement

When a skill (intake, plan, implement, audit, …) finishes, the operator
cannot tell at a glance whether the pane's work-item session ended cleanly,
needs their attention, or failed. The herdr pane title currently shows only
the dispatch context (e.g. `Manually triggered intake`); the end-of-session
state must be surfaced in the pane title itself.

## Users

- **Operator (producer)** watching a grid of herdr panes: wants a zero-click
  visual signal of which sessions are done, need attention, or failed —
  without opening each pane.

Example user stories:

- "As an operator, when a skill completes cleanly I want a green tick at the
  start of the pane title so I can see it finished."
- "As an operator, when a skill completes but left information for my
  attention I want an orange warning so I know to look at it."
- "As an operator, when a skill cannot complete I want a red no-entry sign
  so I know to intervene."

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: When a work-item skill finishes and produces a final report, the herdr
  pane title (label) for the current pane is updated with a status prefix:
  ✅ (or `Done`) when all ACs are met and no substantive producer content
  exists; ⚠️ (or `Note`) when the skill completed but the report contains
  substantive content for the producer's attention; 🚫 (or `Attention`) when
  the skill cannot complete (any unmet/partial/adjusted AC verdict, or
  abort/failure).
- AC2: The prefix is prepended to the existing pane title (e.g.
  `✅ Manually triggered intake`); no colour/ANSI is embedded in the label;
  the update is idempotent (re-running does not stack prefixes).
- AC3: Text fallbacks `Done` / `Note` / `Attention` are used when emoticons
  are not possible (reusing the report's existing `--no-icons` /
  `WL_NO_ICONS=1` mechanism).
- AC4: On skill abort or failure (including abort paths such as
  `intake.py abort`, `implement.py abort`, audit-runner aborts), the pane
  title is set to the red state regardless of whether a final report is
  produced.
- AC5: The update fails gracefully outside a herdr pane (no `HERDR_ENV`,
  `HERDR_PANE_ID`, or herdr CLI unavailable): no crash, no error surfaced to
  the skill run.
- AC6: Full project test suite must pass with the new changes, and all
  related documentation is updated (SKILL.md reports, tests for the new
  helper).

## Constraints

- Not a pi extension — the update is a call to the herdr CLI/API
  (`herdr pane rename <pane_id> <label>`; current pane id from
  `HERDR_PANE_ID` env var; herdr ≥ current installed version).
- Trigger is skill completion (end-of-session report render), not the agent
  harness lifecycle.
- Status is derived from the final report's content: AC verdicts
  (met/unmet/adjusted/partial), Producer Actions, Notes.
- Orange = "audit passed but there is information for the producer's
  attention (not necessarily actions, and certainly not when the next action
  is the standard next action in the workflow)" — i.e. substantive content
  beyond the routine workflow next step.
- Colour requirement dropped for text fallbacks: plain `Done`/`Note`/
  `Attention` prefixes, no colour coding.
- Emoji-vs-text fallback follows the existing report convention
  (`--no-icons` / `WL_NO_ICONS=1`), so both modes stay consistent.

## Existing state

- Every work-item skill ends by rendering a canonical report via
  `skill/report/scripts/render_report.py` (report skill, SA-0MSJ082OY003IQ8S),
  passing AC verdicts, producer actions, notes and next action.
- herdr panes carry a `label` field shown as the pane title, set via
  `herdr pane rename <pane_id> <label>`; current pane is identified by the
  `HERDR_PANE_ID` env var (present in pi sessions launched via herdr; also
  `HERDR_ENV=1` and `HERDR_SOCKET_PATH`).
- `render_report.py` already supports `--no-icons` / `WL_NO_ICONS=1` for
  bracketed-text fallbacks — a precedent for the emoticon/text switch.

## Desired change

- Add a small shared helper (e.g. `skill/shared/herdr_pane.py`) that, given a
  status (`done` | `note` | `attention`) and the current pane context,
  prepends the corresponding prefix (✅/⚠️/🚫 or Done/Note/Attention) to the
  existing pane label via the herdr CLI, idempotently.
- Integrate the helper into `render_report.py`: after the report is rendered,
  derive the status from the supplied AC verdicts, producer actions and notes
  and update the pane title (done/note states; red when any AC verdict is not
  met).
- Hook the red state into abort paths (`intake.py abort`, `implement.py
  abort`, audit runner abort/exit paths) so failures always surface red even
  without a final report.
- Fail open when not in a herdr pane or herdr CLI is missing.

## Key Files

- `skill/report/scripts/render_report.py` — derive status from report inputs
  and call the pane-title helper after rendering.
- `skill/shared/herdr_pane.py` (new) — shared herdr CLI wrapper: resolve
  current pane, read existing label, prepend status prefix idempotently.
- `skill/intake/scripts/intake.py` — abort command sets red pane state.
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — abort path sets red pane state.
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — abort/failure exits set red pane
  state.
- `skill/report/SKILL.md` + `skill/report/tests/test_render_report.py` —
  document and test the status derivation and pane update.

## Risks & assumptions

- **herdr CLI availability:** assume herdr is installed and the pane env vars
  are set in agent panes (true today — pi sessions launched via herdr carry
  `HERDR_ENV`/`HERDR_PANE_ID`). Fail-open behaviour (AC5) mitigates drift.
- **Existing pane title truncation:** herdr truncates long labels to ~60
  chars (`MAX_PANE_TITLE_LENGTH`); the prefix plus existing label must fit
  within the limit — the helper should truncate the combined string the same
  way to keep the title valid.
- **Scope creep:** wiring red-state into *every* skill's abort path is broad;
  the helper centralises the logic so each abort site is a one-liner. Extra
  opportunities (e.g. coloured labels in the herdr UI itself) are recorded as
  follow-up work items, not scope.
- **Verdict vocabulary:** `adjusted`/`partial` verdicts count as "not fully
  met" → red; `met` only → eligible for done/note.

## Related work

- SA-0MSJ082OY003IQ8S — "Standardize skill session end-of-session reporting
  via helper report skill": the report renderer this feature extends.
- ContextHub herdr (sibling repo `packages/herdr`): `pane rename`, pane
  titles (`pane-title.ts`, WL-0MSJ4E8UA005KG9Y), agent-state protocol.
- find-related matches (repo): `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`,
  `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md`, `skill/implement/SKILL.md` — the
  abort/failure paths that must surface the red state; no directly-related
  open work items.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Should this live in the SorraAgents repo as a reusable extension, or be a built-in feature in the pi-coding-agent?" — Answer (user): "It is not a pi extension, it is a call to the herdr CLI/API." Source: interactive reply (intake session).
- Q: "Should the title update happen on agent_settled or agent_end?" — Answer (user): "Triggers by the completion of a skill, not by the agent harness." Source: interactive reply.
- Q: "To detect a producer notification, check needsProducerReview?" — Answer (user): "The final summary from the skill indicates status." Source: interactive reply.
- Q: "What should the complete title look like?" — Answer (user): "Just add the prefix to the existing title." Source: interactive reply.
- Q: "Which herdr command sets the pane title?" — Answer (user): "Don't know — look it up using herdr --help." Research: `herdr pane rename <pane_id> <label>` sets the pane label (pane list `label` field, e.g. `Manually triggered intake`); current pane id from `HERDR_PANE_ID` env var; `herdr pane report-metadata --title` is display-only metadata (not the label). Accepted answer: `herdr pane rename` with `HERDR_PANE_ID`.
- Q: "Status derivation from the final summary?" — Answer (user): "Green is correct; Orange is audit passed but there is information for the producer's attention (not necessarily actions, and certainly not when the next action is the standard next action in the workflow); Red is correct." Source: interactive reply.
- Q: "Where should the herdr call live?" — Answer (user): "(a) inside render_report.py so every skill gets it automatically." Source: interactive reply.
- Q: "Orange trigger precision — substantive content?" — Answer (user): "Substantive content." Source: interactive reply.
- Q: "Red path for aborts?" — Answer (user): "Always show red." Source: interactive reply.
- Q: "Fallback colour mechanics?" — Answer (user): "Drop the colour requirement." Source: interactive reply.

# Audit Stuck in `in_progress` When `run-release` is Aborted

## Problem Statement

When the `run-release` script is aborted (e.g., via Ctrl+C or signal) while the audit gate is running audits on work items, those items are left stuck in the `in_progress` state. The audit runner's `wl update --status in_progress` claim is performed before the try/finally block in `cmd_issue` can catch the abort, and a hard kill (SIGKILL) bypasses Python's finally blocks entirely. This breaks the release pipeline because items stuck in `in_progress` are excluded from the `in_review` candidate query.

## Users

- **Release operator**: Runs `run-release` and needs the pipeline to complete or abort cleanly without manual work-item intervention.
- **Automated agents**: Agents waiting for work items to reach `in_review` stage to proceed with release gating.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Audit runner restores pre-audit status on hard abort**: When the `audit_runner.py` process receives SIGKILL (signal 9) during an audit, it must still restore the work item to its pre-audit state (`completed`/`in_review` or whatever it was before the audit). Since Python cannot catch SIGKILL, the solution must use a subprocess wrapper or a separate watchdog process that observes the audit child's death and restores the captured pre-audit status.
- **AC2 — Audit runner restores status on SIGTERM/SIGINT**: When the `audit_runner.py` process receives SIGTERM or SIGINT, the status restoration must still complete even if killed mid-try-block. Python's default SIGINT handling raises `KeyboardInterrupt`, so the `finally` block in `cmd_issue` covers SIGINT, but the default SIGTERM disposition terminates the process *without* running `finally` blocks. An explicit `SIGTERM`/`SIGINT` handler that performs the cleanup and then re-raises (or restores the default disposition and re-signals) is therefore required for SIGTERM.
- **AC3 — No `in_progress` items left after any abort scenario**: After any termination of `audit_runner.py` (SIGTERM, SIGINT, SIGKILL, or process death), the audited work item must NOT remain in `in_progress` state. This can be verified by checking the work item's status after a forced kill.
- **AC4 — All existing audit tests pass**: The fix must not break any existing audit tests in `skill/audit/tests/`.

## Constraints

- The fix must not introduce new race conditions in concurrent audit scenarios (multiple `audit_runner.py` processes auditing the same or different items).
- The solution must follow existing project conventions: no direct `wl update` outside the audit runner's lifecycle management.
- If a direct Python-level SIGKILL handler is impossible, a wrapper mechanism (e.g., a parent process that monitors the child and cleans up on death) must be used.

## Existing State

- The audit runner (`skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`) sets `in_progress` status in `_phase_gate` (the `wl update ... --status in_progress` claim is issued at `audit_runner.py:8219`; `_phase_gate` starts at line 7938) before entering the main `try/finally` block in `cmd_issue`.
- The `finally` block in `cmd_issue` calls `_apply_terminal_lifecycle` which restores the pre-audit state.
- `check-audit-gate.js` (used by `run-release.js`) invokes `audit_runner.py issue <id>` via `execSync` for each candidate work item.
- When the `run-release` script is aborted, the `execSync` call is terminated, killing the `audit_runner.py` child process.
- If killed with SIGKILL (signal 9), Python's `finally` blocks do not execute, leaving the item in `in_progress`.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — Needs a signal handling mechanism or wrapper to ensure status restoration on hard abort.
- `skill/ship/scripts/check-audit-gate.js` — May need a timeout/abort handler to clean up on termination.
- `skill/audit/tests/` — New tests for abort scenarios.

## Related Work

- **SA-0MSQRZ5N6005WI43**: [test-failure] test-check-audit-gate.mjs / test-close-work-items.mjs / test-run-release.mjs (6 node failures) — failing test (still open, critical priority)
- **SA-0MSBU4OBU005WJNB**: Implement skill: gate implementation on Code Freeze status — uses trap/finally pattern for exit cleanup (relevant pattern to follow)

## Clarifying Questions & Answers

- Q: "Is the abort specifically SIGKILL, or does SIGTERM also fail to restore status?" — Answer (Map): SIGTERM should be handled by Python's finally blocks, but SIGKILL cannot be caught by Python at all. The fix must handle SIGKILL via a wrapper mechanism. Source: interactive reply.
- Q: "Can a wrapper process approach work here?" — Answer (Map): Yes, a parent process that monitors the child and cleans up on death is an acceptable approach. Source: interactive reply.

# Intake Brief: RCA — audit Phase 1 / Phase 2 Reliability

**Work Item:** SA-0MU32H6KY0021SJL

## Headline Summary

Conduct a root cause analysis of why the audit pipeline (Phase 1 screening and Phase 2 deep analysis) frequently fails or degrades, quantify the failure modes from debug logs and stored audit reports, and produce a prioritised set of reliability recommendations with follow-up work items.

## Problem Statement

Audits routinely report `Ready to close: No` for *infrastructure* reasons rather than genuine code defects — concurrency saturation aborting Phase 1 parent screens, wall-clock budget exhaustion silently skipping children, a misleading `parse_failure` debug label that fires on successful calls, and in-main-slot child screens left pending. This forces manual re-audits and blocks releases. No single RCA quantifies these modes or ranks fixes.

## Users

- **Release operator** running an automated audit: needs reliable verdicts without manual re-audits.
- **Producer** reviewing audit results: needs trustworthy signals to make release decisions.
- **Agent** running audits: needs predictable behaviour and actionable failure diagnostics.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A written RCA quantifies failure modes from at least 30 days of evidence, grouped by phase (Phase 1 parent, Phase 1 child, Phase 2 parent deep, Phase 2 child deep, false-positive screen) and by root cause, with reproducible commands/queries and representative examples.
2. The RCA explicitly confirms or refutes **F1** (the `parse_failure` label fires on successful calls) and states the effect on observability; it must distinguish label noise from genuine parse failures.
3. Every failure mode in the RCA is backed by a count and at least one concrete example (item id + log path or report excerpt).
4. A prioritised recommendation list is produced (impact × effort), each item naming the concrete change, the expected reliability effect, and the observable signal that would confirm improvement.
5. Recommendations cover, at minimum: JSON-output contract robustness (e.g. JSON-first prompting / schema retry / fenced-block tolerant parsing), timeout and wall-clock budget right-sizing, concurrency saturation and queue-wait policy, child-audit execution strategy (in-main-slot vs separate-process), provider-error retry policy, and debug-log observability (a correct, non-misleading reason taxonomy).
6. Each accepted recommendation is captured as a follow-up work item (child of this item or `discovered-from`) with its own testable ACs; rejected recommendations record the rationale.
7. UK English throughout; no code changes are required by this item other than producing the RCA/recommendations (implementation lands via the follow-ups).

## Constraints

- Read-only analysis of logs and stored reports; do not modify the audit runner as part of this item.
- Use bounded reads for large log stores (stream, filter by context/reason); never unbounded recursive grep over `.worklog/`.
- Do not close or reopen unrelated work items; link to the prior art below instead.

## Evidence Sources

1. **Debug corpus:** `~/.audit_debug/SorraAgents/audit_debug_*.jsonl` (91 files analysed; raw Pi streams + the logged `reason` field).
2. **Stored audit reports:** `wl show` worklog data (rawOutput per item; counts from 2026-09-15 export).
3. **Runner source:** `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` (`_call_pi`, `_call_pi_and_maybe_log`, `_extract_json_array`, Phase 1/Phase 2 call sites).
4. **Log files:** `~/.audit_debug/SorraAgents/*.log` (audit runs with verdicts and diagnostics).

## Preliminary Findings (to be verified and extended)

### F1 — The debug-log `reason: parse_failure` label is misleading (observability bug)

**Confirmed.** Code inspection of `_call_pi_and_maybe_log` (L4828) shows:

```python
elif isinstance(result, dict) and (result.get("raw_stdout") or result.get("raw_stderr")):
    reason = "provider_error" if result.get("_provider_error") else "parse_failure"
```

The label fires whenever `raw_stdout` or `raw_stderr` is present — which is true on **every** successful call. Corpus analysis of 91 JSONL debug files shows:

- 91 files, all containing `parse_failure` entries as the dominant reason.
- Only 5 files contain `provider_error` (total: ~10 provider_error entries across the corpus).
- Only 2 files contain `debug_log` entries (explicit debug log path was provided).

The preliminary finding of ~92–95% false-positive rate is confirmed — the `parse_failure` label is an observability bug that invalidates any failure analysis keyed on it.

### F2 — Genuine JSON-contract failures are real but rare (~5–8%)

**To be verified.** The preliminary finding cites 34 genuine failures in 285 real-project logs. This count requires verification against the actual debug corpus — checking which `parse_failure` entries actually contain unparseable content vs. parseable content mislabelled by the F1 bug.

### F3 — Wall-clock budget exhaustion dominates (child skips + Phase 2 timeouts)

**Confirmed in log files.** Multiple log entries show:
- "pending deep code review (Phase 1 blocked)" — Phase 2 skipped after Phase 1 detected blocking issues.
- Parent-process timeout budgets vary widely (~120s, 900s, 1500s, 3110s) — inconsistent right-sizing.
- Stored report data (from prior audit): `Skipped due to audit timeout` ~176, `Audit runner skipped this child after Ns` ~100+.

### F4 — Concurrency saturation aborts Phase 1

**Confirmed.** Log files show repeated "Audit concurrency limit reached: audit concurrency queue 'audit' saturated: no slot within 90s" and "Audit concurrency limit reached: semaphore 'audit' busy: no slot free within 0.0s (max_workers=1)". Phase 1 parent screens return `unmet` with zero Pi calls made.

### F5 — In-main-slot child screens leave children unverified

**Confirmed in log files.** Multiple entries show "pending deep code review (Phase 1 blocked)" — child ACs left in `partial (pending main-session review)` state when the main session does not run the emitted `[AUDIT_IN_MAIN_SLOT_WORK]` prompts.

### F6 — Provider errors

**Confirmed.** Corpus analysis: ~10 `provider_error` entries across 91 files (SA-0MSL1Z70C007B9VZ: 3, SA-0MSM6VU2K001IMVP: 1, SA-0MSUT8GQP004WSYN: 1, SA-0MSNYMKV7005P0H9: 1, SA-0MU8EKJYY007PT42: 1). Provider errors are currently conflated with the misleading `parse_failure` label.

| SA-0MSQ7MQEJ0064ZB0 | Motivating audit (2026-09-15) | — | Source of this RCA |

## Existing State

The audit runner (`audit_runner.py`) has 10+ call sites for `_call_pi_and_maybe_log`. The debug-log reason taxonomy is set in a single branch (L4906) but is overly broad. The `_extract_json_array` parser exists but does not handle fenced blocks or prose-prefixed JSON consistently. Concurrency is managed via a priority queue with `max_workers=2` (configurable). Wall-clock budgets are set ad-hoc across multiple call sites.

A comprehensive RCA documenting all failure modes with quantified counts, examples, and reproducible queries — followed by a prioritised recommendation list that feeds into the already-created follow-up work items (R1–R7).

# Intake: Audit-runner pi calls crash with `Connection error.` from stale-ctx extension exceptions

## Problem statement

Audit-runner `pi` subprocesses crash mid-call and the runner records
`provider_error: Connection error.` because pi extensions loaded into the audit
session throw on a **stale `ExtensionContext`** after pi replaces or reloads the
session. The **fatal uncaught exception** is thrown by the ContextHub-owned
`worklog` recovery extension (`register-recovery.ts`, `_notifyFn` →
`ctx.ui.notify`), not by `pi-client/proxy-compaction-bridge`. Two
SorraAgents-owned extensions (`proxy-compaction-bridge` and `proxy-sse-signals`)
throw the *same* stale-ctx error but pi catches those and prints them as
(non-fatal) `Extension error (...)` lines. This blocks audits and therefore the
ship final-validation gate (exit 12).

## Users

- **Release manager** — needs audits to complete so `dev` → `main` is not blocked
  by spurious provider failures.
  - *As a release manager, I want an audit pi call to return a genuine verdict
    even after an extension-triggered session replacement, so the release gate
    is not blocked by an infrastructure crash.*
- **Audit operator** — needs `provider_error` entries in the debug corpus to
  reflect real provider faults, not extension crashes.
  - *As an audit operator, I want the audit debug log to distinguish a real
    provider fault from an extension exception, so I can triage correctly.*
- **Pi extension maintainer** — needs extensions to fail safe when the session
  they were registered against is replaced.
  - *As a maintainer, I want my extension's async callbacks to no-op when the
    captured ctx is invalid, so a session swap cannot crash an unrelated run.*

## Existing state (evidence)

The failure was captured for the audit of **SA-0MSRWAY9A005Q0CB** (now deleted).
The debug log `~/.audit_debug/SorraAgents/audit_debug_SA-0MSRWAY9A005Q0CB.jsonl`
(`context=parent`) records:

- `reason: provider_error`, `provider_error: "Connection error."`,
  `elapsed_seconds: ~713`.
- `raw_stderr` contains one `Extension error
  (/home/rgardler/.pi/agent/extensions/proxy-compaction-bridge/index.ts): This
  extension ctx is stale ...` line, one identical line for
  `proxy-sse-signals`, and then the **fatal, uncaught** trace:

  ```
  Error: This extension ctx is stale after session replacement or reload. ...
      at ExtensionRunner.assertActive (...)
      at get ui (...)
      at _notifyFn (/home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub/packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/register-recovery.ts:71:41)
      at _notifyRetryAttempt (.../register-recovery.ts:549:5)
      at triggerInvisibleContinue (.../register-recovery.ts:391:7)
      at process.processTicksAndRejections (...)
  Node.js v22.22.1
  ```

  The trailing `Node.js v22.22.1` banner shows the pi process **crashed**; the
  audit runner then surfaced `Connection error.` from the pi JSON stream.

Corpus scan across every `reason=provider_error` entry
(`~/.audit_debug/SorraAgents/audit_debug_*.jsonl`) shows **all** non-empty
`raw_stderr` provider errors carry the `register-recovery.ts` stale-ctx stack;
some also carry the `proxy-compaction-bridge` / `proxy-sse-signals`
`Extension error` lines (non-fatal, caught by pi).

Root cause of each stale access:

- `ContextHub .../register-recovery.ts` — `_notifyFn` is assigned a closure over
  the *handler's* `ctx` (`_notifyFn = (message, level) => ctx.ui.notify(...)`,
  lines ~84/87/212) and is later invoked from the async retry loop
  (`_notifyRetryAttempt` → `_notifyFn`). If the session was replaced/reloaded in
  between, `ctx.ui` throws — and because the call originates in a timer/async
  callback, pi never catches it and the process dies.
- `pi-client/proxy-compaction-bridge/index.ts` — both `after_provider_response`
  and `context` handlers call `ctx.sessionManager.getSessionId()` on the event
  ctx; a stale ctx throws.
- `pi-client/proxy-sse-signals/index.ts` — `turn_start` captures `ctx.ui` as
  `statusUi`; the capturing-fetch callback later calls `statusUi.setStatus(...)`
  on the stale UI handle.

`pi` supports `--no-extensions` / `-ne` (disables extension discovery), alongside
the `--no-context-files --no-skills` flags the audit runner already adds to
`_call_pi`. Audit prompts are read-only and fully self-contained, so they do not
depend on extensions.

## Desired change

1. **Unblock audit calls (SorraAgents-owned):** stop loading interactive/UI
   extensions in audit-runner pi subprocesses — add `--no-extensions` to the
   `_call_pi` command (mirroring the existing context-reduction flags).
2. **Harden the SorraAgents-owned extensions:** make `proxy-compaction-bridge`
   and `proxy-sse-signals` fail safe on a stale/replaced ctx — never call
   `ctx.ui`/`ctx.sessionManager` on an invalidated ctx (guard, re-capture from a
   fresh handler, or no-op/passthrough).
3. **Fatal crash (cross-repo handoff — delivered):** the ContextHub
   `worklog` recovery-extension stale-ctx crash is handed off to
   **WL-0MUIV50EJ007VH9B** (`Worklog recovery extension crashes pi on stale
   ExtensionContext after session replacement (_notifyFn)`), which is not edited
   from this SorraAgents work item.

## Acceptance criteria

1. **No extension crash on audit calls:** the audit runner's `_call_pi` command
   excludes extension discovery (`--no-extensions`). Verified by a unit test
   asserting the constructed command (both tool-enabled and tool-disabled paths).
2. **Stale-ctx-safe SorraAgents extensions:** `proxy-compaction-bridge` and
   `proxy-sse-signals` no-op (context passthrough / status unchanged) when their
   handler or async callback observes an invalidated `ctx`, never throwing.
   Verified by `node:test` unit tests injecting a stale-ctx stub.
3. **Re-audit completes genuinely:** a re-audit of SA-0MSRWAY9A005Q0CB (or an
   equivalent audit pi call that triggers a session replacement) completes with a
   genuine verdict (`met`/`partial`/`adjusted`) and the debug entry's `reason` is
   not `provider_error` with `Connection error.` attributable to an extension
   exception.
4. **Regression tests:** a stale/replaced-session-ctx regression test exists for
   both `pi-client` extensions (Node unit tests) and a Python test asserts the
   audit `_call_pi` command includes `--no-extensions`; the tests fail against
   the pre-fix code.
5. **Docs + full suite:** `docs/dev/proxy-compaction-bridge.md` and
   `docs/dev/audit-reliability-rca.md` (F6) are updated to reflect the corrected
   attribution/fix; all related documentation (code comments, README, docs) is
   updated; and the full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Cross-repo boundary:** the fatal crash is in
  `/home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub` (separate repo and `WL-` worklog). It is
  **not** edited from this item; the fix is tracked in WL-0MUIV50EJ007VH9B.
- **Do not regress** the compaction-bridge wire contract
  (LP-0MTYGZ1DI0004QP8) or the dispatch reshape semantics/tests.
- **Do not weaken fail-closed audit behaviour**; the audit runner must still
  return `unmet`/`partial` on genuine provider errors, not mask them.
- `--no-extensions` affects all discovered extensions in audit calls only; the
  interactive TUI extension behaviour (compaction mirroring, status line,
  recovery) must remain unchanged.
- `wl`-tracked, test-first, build → test → commit.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `_call_pi` builds the pi command
  (~L3648); add `--no-extensions`.
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_core.py` — command-flag tests (~L267–304);
  add the `--no-extensions` assertion.
- `pi-client/proxy-compaction-bridge/index.ts` — guard/re-bind the session id
  used by `after_provider_response` and `context` handlers.
- `pi-client/proxy-compaction-bridge/compaction-bridge.js` — pure core (no ctx
  access); keep behaviour, extend tests only.
- `pi-client/proxy-sse-signals/index.ts` — guard the captured `statusUi` used by
  the capturing-fetch callback.
- `tests/unit/test_compaction-bridge.mjs`,
  `tests/unit/test-proxy-sse-signals.mjs` — stale-ctx regression coverage.
- `docs/dev/proxy-compaction-bridge.md`, `docs/dev/audit-reliability-rca.md` —
  documentation/correction.
- *(cross-repo, tracked in WL-0MUIV50EJ007VH9B)*
  `/home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub/packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/register-recovery.ts`.

## Related work (manual)

- **SA-0MSRWAY9A005Q0CB** — `[test-failure] getCompletedOrInReviewItems ...`
  (`discovered-from`; the audit that failed with this signature; now deleted).
- **SA-0MU2OY1N9000XL2H** — Ship skill: parent-coverage and out-of-scope rules for
  child audits in the final-validation gate (records the same failure as the
  motivation for removing manual interruptions).
- **SA-0MU32H6KY0021SJL** — RCA: Audit Pipeline Reliability
  (`docs/dev/audit-reliability-rca.md`); F6 documents the 9 `provider_error`
  entries (incl. `Connection error.`) and their conflation with parse failures.
- **SA-0MTYGZIWF000ZLU0** — origin of `proxy-compaction-bridge` (wire contract
  LP-0MTYGZ1DI0004QP8).
- **SA-0MSHAKSEA001LQ6T** — origin of `proxy-sse-signals`.
- **SA-0MSISKM8F004NW1U** — audit context reduction
  (`--no-context-files --no-skills`); precedent for adding a loader flag to
  `_call_pi`.
- **WL-0MUIV50EJ007VH9B** (ContextHub) — handoff item for the fatal
  `register-recovery.ts` stale-ctx crash.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 (scope/cross-repo).** Debug-log evidence shows the *fatal* uncaught
  exception is thrown by the ContextHub-owned `worklog` extension
  (`register-recovery.ts`), not `pi-client/proxy-compaction-bridge`. How should
  this item be scoped?
  - Answer (producer): **(c) analysis/handoff** — do not edit ContextHub from this
    item; **create a `WL-` item** for the fatal `register-recovery` crash, and do
    the SorraAgents-side extensions/audit fixes + tests here.
  - Evidence: created **WL-0MUIV50EJ007VH9B** in ContextHub; SorraAgents-side
    work captured in the ACs above (consistent with Q3 = (a), which names tests
    for the `pi-client` extensions and the audit `--no-extensions` command).
- **Q2 (audit extension policy).** Is disabling extension discovery for
  audit-runner pi calls (`pi ... --no-extensions`, alongside
  `--no-context-files --no-skills`) acceptable?
  - Answer (producer): **n/a** — not separately decided; Q3(a) explicitly names
    the `--no-extensions` command assertion, so it is in scope (AC1/AC4).
- **Q3 (regression-test surface).** Where should the stale-ctx regression test
  live?
  - Answer (producer): **(a)** Node unit tests for both `pi-client` extensions

# Intake Brief: child-audit cascade can recursively execute the full suite (cold cache / concurrent runs)

## Problem Statement

A full-suite run can enter unbounded recursion when the test cache is cold (e.g.
a fresh worktree/commit) and/or another full-suite run is executing
concurrently. An audit test spawns a **real** `audit_runner.py issue` child
subprocess; that child audit's automatic full-suite execution (F3) hits a cache
miss and executes the real pytest suite, which re-runs the same test, which
spawns another real child audit — and so on until the outer timeout (observed
1500s+ and 19–50+ nested processes). The per-run child cap
(`--max-child-audits`) does not bound this because it resets in every child
process.

## Users & User Stories

- **Agent / operator:** "When I run the full suite (`run_tests.py --scope full`)
  or `implement.py finish` from a cold cache, it must complete in bounded time
  — no runaway nesting that blows the timeout."
- **Reviewer / producer:** "A child-audit cascade must never re-enter the full
  suite; if it would, it must fail fast with a clear diagnostic rather than
  hanging the release gate."
- **Future maintainer:** "Audit tests that exercise the child-cascade path must
  never spawn a real child audit, and there must be a documented convention and
  a regression test that keeps it that way."

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Cold-cache full-suite completion:** `run_tests.py --scope full`
  completes (no recursion) from a **cold** test cache in a fresh
  `implement.py start` worktree. *Verification:* clear the cache / start a fresh
  worktree, run the suite, and confirm a single suite invocation (no nested
  `audit_runner.py issue … --force` → `pytest` chain) with no timeout.
- **AC2 — Recursion guard (bounded, fails fast):** an audit's automatic
  full-suite execution (F3) cannot itself trigger another automatic full-suite
  execution. When a suite run is already owned by an ancestor process, a nested
  audit stands down (or the cascade is depth-capped) and emits a clear
  diagnostic; execution-dependent ACs stay partial/fail-open. *Verification:* a
  dedicated regression test simulates a child-audit cascade with a cold cache
  and asserts no nested suite execution occurs and the run returns promptly.
- **AC3 — Test isolation preserved:** `TestChildPersistFailureFatal` (and any
  other audit test that reaches the child-audit subprocess) mocks the
  child-audit subprocess, so no real `audit_runner.py issue` child is spawned —
  while still asserting its intended behaviour (non-zero rc, plus
  `Failed to persist audit for child …` and `Aborting` on stderr).
  *Verification:* the class's tests pass in isolation and in the full suite; the
  test asserts the (mocked) child invocation rather than real execution.
- **AC4 — Production behaviour preserved:** outside a nested/test suite-run
  context, a standalone audit's F3 automatic full-suite execution is unchanged.
  *Verification:* existing F3 tests remain green, plus a new test proving a
  standalone audit still auto-executes on a cold cache.
- **AC5 — Documentation updated:** `skill/audit/SKILL.md`,
  `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md`, and the shared test-writing guidance
  document the recursion guard, the ancestor-ownership rule, and the
  "mock the child-audit subprocess in tests" convention. All related
  documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments,
  README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- **AC6 — Full project test suite passes** with the new changes, both
  sequentially and from a cold cache, with zero new regressions; no test is
  skipped, xfailed, or retried to reach green. (CHANGELOG.md is excluded — it is
  managed by the ship skill's release pipeline.)

## Constraints

- **Do not weaken production child-audit behaviour.** A standalone audit must
  keep the F3 auto-execution behaviour; the guard applies only to nested /
  test auto-run contexts.
- **Reuse existing nesting machinery where possible.** Prefer the existing
  ancestor-ownership marker (`LIVE_REPO_GUARD_ACTIVE`, set by `run_tests.py`
  while it owns the checkout) or an analogous audit-specific marker propagated
  into child-audit subprocesses, rather than new bespoke state.
- **Keep the per-run child cap intact.** `--max-child-audits` /
  `AUDIT_MAX_CHILD_AUDITS` (SA-0MSKB6V5Q007YDHE) remains; the new guard
  addresses cross-process depth, which the per-process cap cannot.
- **No global sleeps, no whole-suite serialisation, no single-worker
  requirement.**
- **Minimal blast radius:** change shared helpers only where required; re-verify
  the full suite if a shared helper changes.
- **Worktree discipline:** implementation happens in the `implement.py start`
  worktree; never push to `main`.

## Existing State

- `TestChildPersistFailureFatal` (`skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_launch_context.py:631`)
  calls `audit_runner.cmd_issue(..., audit_children=True)` with a faked `wl`
  runner but **no mock of `audit_runner.subprocess.run`**, so the child-audit
  spawn at `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py:~10040` runs for real.
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_children.py` already mocks
  `subprocess.run` (4 sites); `test_audit_runner_core.py` likewise. Other
  `audit_children=True` call sites pass a canned `child_audit_raw` or otherwise
  bypass the spawn, but this must be re-audited during implementation.
- Auto-execution path: `cmd_issue` → `_auto_green_run_outcome` (cache
  classification) → on `_FULL_SUITE_CACHE_MISS` →
  `_run_tests_via_test_skill` (`audit_runner.py:2465`) →
  `run_cached(full_suite_commands(...), force=True)` (`skill/test_cache.py:341`).
  `run_cached` does not go through `run_tests.py`.
- `LIVE_REPO_GUARD_ACTIVE` (`skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py:116`,
  `skill/shared/live_repo_guard.py:45`) is set by `run_tests.py` while it owns
  the checkout and is inherited by subprocesses; nested `run_tests.py`/pytest
  stand down, but the audit auto-execution path does not consult it.
- The per-run child-audit cap (`AUDIT_MAX_CHILD_AUDITS`, default 5,
  `audit_runner.py:544`) is per-process, so cross-process depth is unbounded.
- Observed evidence: `implement.py finish` timed out after 1500s; a plain
  `run_tests.py --scope full` also timed out (>1500s). The offending test
  passes in isolation (2 passed in 1.44s); the full suite passes sequentially
  on a warm cache (350s, 2743 passed).

## Desired Change

1. Gate the audit's F3 auto-execution on ancestor suite ownership: when a suite
   run is already in progress in an ancestor process (reuse
   `LIVE_REPO_GUARD_ACTIVE` or an analogous marker propagated into the
   child-audit command), stand down with a clear diagnostic and leave
   execution-dependent ACs partial (fail-open) instead of executing a nested
   suite.
2. Mock the child-audit subprocess in `TestChildPersistFailureFatal._run_with_child`
   (and re-audit every `cmd_issue(audit_children=True)` test site), preserving
   the class's persist-failure assertions.
3. Add a regression test proving a child-audit cascade cannot re-enter the full
   suite (bounded, fast fail).
4. Document the guard and the test-mocking convention.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — Gate the F3 cache-miss auto-execution
  branch (~L8044-8070) on ancestor suite ownership; propagate the marker into
  the child-audit command (~L10002-10045).
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_launch_context.py` — Mock
  `audit_runner.subprocess.run` in `TestChildPersistFailureFatal._run_with_child`
  (L631-790); keep the persist-failure assertions.
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_children.py` — Reference pattern for
  mocking `subprocess.run`; add/adjust the cascade-bounded regression test.
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — `LIVE_REPO_GUARD_ACTIVE` definition/usage
  (L116, ~L1774); confirm/extend semantics if reused.
- `skill/shared/live_repo_guard.py` — `MARKER_ENV` definition (L45) if the
  marker is shared.
- `skill/test_cache.py` — `run_cached(force=True)` (L341) if the guard is
  centralised there rather than in `audit_runner`.
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md`, `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md`,
  `skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md` — Document the guard and the
  test-mocking convention.

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Assumption:** the runaway loop is the real child-audit `subprocess.run`
  (`audit_runner.py:~10040`), which resolves `full_suite_commands()` against the
  repository cwd and force-executes on a cold cache. The parent audit's own
  auto-execution resolves against the patched temp target root (no suite), so
  mocking the child spawn plus adding the guard breaks the chain.
- **Assumption:** production dispatch never runs a standalone audit nested
  inside `run_tests.py`, so the ancestor-ownership guard has no effect on
  production audit behaviour (AC4).
- **Risk:** reusing `LIVE_REPO_GUARD_ACTIVE` could suppress legitimate
  auto-execution if the marker leaks across processes; mitigate by setting and
  clearing it in a `finally`, as `run_tests.py` already does.
- **Risk:** the guard makes execution-dependent ACs partial for nested audits;
  this is fail-open (never a degraded "met" verdict) and acceptable.
- **Risk:** other tests may still spawn real child audits that only surface
  under a cold cache; mitigate by re-auditing every
  `cmd_issue(audit_children=True)` call site (AC3).
- **Risk (scope creep):** the concurrency-semaphore bypass is a distinct
  defect; recorded as discovered-from SA-0MUJK94QN0015925 rather than folded
  into this item.

## Related Work

- **SA-0MSKB6V5Q007YDHE** (completed) — opt-in child audit cascade with a
  per-run cap; the cap is per-process and does not bound cross-process depth.
- **SA-0MSTN5KRF0097TVP** (F3 auto-execution hatch) — introduced automatic
  suite execution on a cache miss; this item must bound it without weakening
  the standalone case.
- **SA-0MSIU5HFI0024D7W** (completed) — automatic read-only full-suite
  verification (cache consumption).
- **SA-0MSJELSWS002UF60** (completed) — `--run-tests` execution; noted that

- **discovered-from:SA-0MNCDAQ8W008KOG9** — the find-related v3 review during
  which this defect was found.
- **SA-0MTHC710X003ORZM** (completed) — audit staleness race (adjacent audit
  freshness/staleness behaviour).

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items

- **SA-0MRMCK0C8008ESE0** – [test-failure] test_audit_skill_doc.py::TestAuditSkillWorkItemIdDetection::test_scan_match_branch_structure — failing test (completed)
